additional_info.subject: Sandy Road – on-site charging failure experienced by operator on chargers 3304 and 3303 (evening of 21 January)
additional_info.body:
Dear Siemens Support Team,
We are raising a new support request relating to an issue personally experienced by me on site this evening at our Sandy Road location. This is a fresh incident and is separate from previous cases.
Site details
Location Sandy Road, Galway, Ireland
ChargePoint IDs
IE-GFX-E170003304
IE-GFX-E170003303
Context
At the time of arrival this evening, charger 3303 already had one connector set to Unavailable, as previously requested. I required a charge and therefore proceeded first to charger 3304.
On-site test and observed behaviour
On 21 January 2026, between approximately 17:44 and 17:50 UTC, the following occurred.
• I first attempted to start a charging session on charger 3304, using the Charge Assist app. I did not use contactless card payment.
• Multiple start attempts were made. Each attempt resulted in the app taking a pre-authorisation, but the charging session did not start.
• During these attempts, charging did not progress beyond the initial stages and no energy delivery occurred.
I then moved to charger 3303.
• On charger 3303, I connected to the connector that remained available.
• The charger entered Preparation state but did not progress to Charging.
• The connector remained locked in the vehicle while the charger stalled. I waited, then stopped the process and attempted again.
• Multiple attempts were made on this charger, with the same outcome. Charging did not start.
As I required a charge, I then moved to charger 3302.
• On charger 3302, using the same vehicle, app, and start procedure, the charging session started immediately on the first attempt and charged normally.
Additional observation
While on site, I noted that charger 3304 displayed a session amount of approximately €12 on the payment terminal screen, which appeared to remain displayed and did not clear in the normal way. This amount appeared low for a completed DC session and did not appear to correspond to an active or progressing charge at the time. We are unsure whether this reflects a session that did not close correctly.
Log context
Reviewing the logs subsequently, charger 3304 shows multiple transitions to Unavailable earlier in the day, consistent with the issues experienced on site this evening. Relevant Unavailable and Faulted status updates for this charger were recorded earlier on 21 January.
Impact
This issue was experienced directly by me as the operator. If this behaviour is occurring for the site owner, it is highly likely that it is also affecting customers, potentially without all incidents being reported. The pattern of issues observed at Sandy Road over the past day is concerning.
Request
We request urgent Siemens assistance this evening to:
• Review charger and connector logs for 3304 and 3303 between 17:44 and 17:50 UTC on 21 January 2026
• Identify why accepted app-based pre-authorisations are not progressing to started charging sessions
• Review the stalled Preparation state observed on charger 3303
• Review the session amount remaining displayed on charger 3304 and confirm whether a session may not have closed correctly
• Advise on immediate next steps and whether on-site intervention is required
Please treat this as urgent, given the direct customer impact and the inability to reliably charge at this site.
Kind regards,
Colin
Colin Barry
Brite EV charging

Just to clarify our expectation on this type of request, when we raise an issue after a physical on-site incident and after checking our own backend logs, we are not asking for a confirmation of the current live status. A live screenshot only tells us the charger’s present state and does not address whether any faults, warnings, protective events or internal resets occurred in the period leading up to the incident.
What we need from Siemens, as the OEM, is a clear historical confirmation for the defined window. Specifically, for the 24 hours preceding the reported issue

additional_info.body:
Hi Colin, good morning.
I will start with yesterday's reported problem at around 11:56. I believe that this is the problem that the customer reported:
What I see is that the customer didn't provide any authentication for a few mins and the session stopped.
The next session on DC2 worked completely well and there was no reboot or similar, inbetween.
For this reported issue from today, I searched for 3301 and 3302 and I cannot find any failed session, I searched both since 3 am, as I can see from your email it came at 7am.
In 3301 I only find one session and it's successfull:
In 3302 there is no attempt at all, the charger doesn't even recognize if there was any EV plugged in, we usually see it with this log:
And in 3302 I only have a session start at this time and works perfectly:
Is it possible that it's a different charger? Also, if the session fails and there is no energy transfer from our side, it's a clear issue on the Payment Terminal provider service and not related to us. To confirm this I need your help finding the session.
Please also be aware that I really want to support you in this topic but it's not related to the initial reported issue and should be refered in a new ticket, as the documentation will be scattered.
I will keep working with this ticket but in the future please open a new ticket :)
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
